plant.culled_by: TWO INDEPENDENT EYES. Rafe, device walk, 2026-09-06; and round 30's blind seat, 2026-09-06.
plant.verbatim: flat pale block, no interior texture (seat) / too shiny on worn areas, character washed out (Rafe)

seat.BEST_WHY: The masonry survives its own lighting. At 8× on the floor left of the figure (x 300–440, y 440–560) the vertical joint at x≈352 and the horizontals at y≈477 and y≈518 are intact and 1px wide *through* the brightest part of the pool — the light raises the stone's value without dissolving its cut. The joints also vary: the block at (330–390, 480–518) has a chipped lower-left corner and a scuffed face, the one beside it at (395–450, 480–518) is clean, so they read as laid stones rather than one stamped tile. The figure is lit by the lamp he is carrying — there is a distinct pale rim on the right of the helmet and a bright yellow highlight on the cheek at (410–416, 472–478), and the shield holds four separate tones (cream face, warmer ring, dark boss slot, outline) so it stays a shield against a floor of nearly the same brightness. That last part is the actual craft: separating a cream object from a cream ground by structure instead of by value.
seat.WORST_WHY: Two cameras in one frame, and a floor that is a noise layer. The barrels at (112–142, 192–215) and (163–193, 192–215) are drawn in three-quarter side view — you can see the staved front face and the vertical hoop *and* the lid ellipse at once — while the flagstones, the crates' footprints and the water are straight top-down. They are also pixel-identical duplicates placed side by side, and neither casts a shadow; the left one's base lands exactly on the dirt/stone seam at y=214 with a hard cut and no contact. The dirt field (x 56–343, y 0–214) is one flat mid-brown with randomly scattered dark-red 1px specks and a steel-blue two-pixel chip reused about a dozen times (x≈133 y≈9, x≈180 y≈76, x≈183 y≈157, x≈219 y≈124) floating with no shadow — no grid, no repeat structure, no direction of wear. Its boundary against the cobble is a raw 1px cut: dead straight down x=56 from y=0 to y=214, then dead straight along y=214 to x=343, with no transition tile and no scatter across the seam. The pond (248–343, 0–190) is an axis-aligned rectangle with square corners, flat teal, no shoreline and no depth. And there is no lighting model at all — the far corners are exactly as bright as the centre.

flip_list: The figure carrying the only light is darker than the ground he stands on: his shield samples L≈139 and his face L≈127 against floor L≈207 immediately to his right. Invert that — the sprite must be the brightest thing in its own pool, above the floor value, not 70 below it.

The lamp casts no light onto its bearer. At 8× the face (404–414, 472–482) is one solid brick-orange mass with a single lighter smudge and no rim. Restore the pale helmet rim and the cheek highlight so the light source is legible on the figure holding it.

The shield at (414–425, 483–497) has collapsed from four tones to two — a flat brown slab with one 4px dark dash. Re-separate the boss, the ring and the face; a shield that reads as a disc of cardboard at play size is the player's own avatar failing.
Boots, belt and torso have converged to near-identical mid-orange, so the legs merge into the body. Push the boots at least 30 luma below the tunic.

The wall band at (200–440, 395–450) is built from the same flagstone rectangles at the same joint pitch as the floor at (200–440, 460–520), differing only in value. Give the wall a different block size or bond pattern, plus a top surface and a cast shadow onto the floor at its base, so it is architecture and not floor-in-shadow.

The corridor mouth at (503–535, 400–455) has no wall across it: the pale corridor floor runs down into the pale room floor with a single 1px value step at y≈440. Draw the wall through the junction and let the doorway be a cut in it.

The right-hand wall at (535–585, 240–440) is soft cloudy blobs with no joints, sitting 60px from floor tiles with crisp 1px joints. Match the level of finish — either the walls get joints or the floor loses them.

panel.ruling: majority of three independent blind seats rank the build above approved_capture, no unrouted flags from any; each seat its own axis-matched plant. — Rafe, 2026-09-08
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
item_exit.item: #198 — the lamp-core halo: a soft blur around the player with no edge and no cause
item_exit.claim: the halo is the floor losing RELATIVE CONTRAST where the light is strongest, the two terms responsible are named by null control, and the larger one now carries the stone's own value instead of adding a flat wash
item_exit.measured: Named by null control, as mean|grad| / mean luminance over floor cells, core (0.5-1.2 tiles) against mid-field (2.0-2.8): as shipped 0.677, shoulder nulled 0.819, specular nulled 0.858. The two signatures differ and that is what identifies them — nulling the SHOULDER lifts absolute variation and the mean together (|grad| 7.72 -> 11.03, mean 156 -> 173), a compression released; nulling the SPECULAR barely moves absolute variation while dropping the mean a fifth (|grad| 7.72 -> 8.63, mean 156 -> 124), a term adding light without adding texture. FIX, on the larger term: the specular is scaled by the fragment's own value normalised by the family's median albedo, so it is proportional rather than additive and Weber contrast survives it. Core relative contrast 0.0572 -> 0.0651 (+13.8%), halo ratio 0.677 -> 0.722, at 0.8% of mean delivered floor value (89.115 -> 88.424) — the magnitude is preserved and only its distribution moves, so #184's measured specular share is not quietly retuned. NULL EXACT: spec_shade 0.0 reproduces the previous build byte-for-byte (sha256 839fb12f6ff4 on both), which is what confines the change to this term.
item_exit.instrument: null-control arms on the shipped scene (MANIFEST material overrides, throwaway); relative local contrast by radial ring, floor cells only

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
